intro: Binary ↔ Text converts text into 8-bit binary and back, using UTF-8 byte encoding. Encode mode turns each character into space-separated bytes, while decode mode reads space-separated binary groups and reconstructs the original text. It's handy for learning how characters map to bits, debugging byte-level data, or preparing simple binary representations.
useCases: Encode a string into space-separated 8-bit binary to see its UTF-8 byte representation
Decode a binary sequence back into readable text
Inspect how multi-byte characters (emoji, accented letters) are encoded in UTF-8
Teach or learn the relationship between characters, bytes, and bits
Verify or hand-craft binary payloads while debugging low-level data

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser using the standard TextEncoder and TextDecoder APIs. Nothing you type is uploaded or stored on a server.

faq.q: What binary format does it produce?
faq.a: Encoding outputs each byte as exactly 8 bits, zero-padded, with bytes separated by a single space (for example 'A' becomes 01000001).

faq.q: How should input be formatted when decoding?
faq.a: Provide binary digits in groups separated by whitespace. Each group must contain 1 to 8 of only the characters 0 and 1; anything else triggers an 'Invalid binary byte' error.

faq.q: How are non-ASCII characters like emoji handled?
faq.a: Text is encoded as UTF-8, so characters outside ASCII produce multiple bytes. For example a single emoji becomes several space-separated 8-bit groups.

faq.q: Can I decode binary that isn't separated by spaces?
faq.a: No. Decoding splits on whitespace, so a continuous string of bits won't be parsed into bytes. Separate each byte with a space.
